title: Spire Mod Manager (Beta)
description:
Spire Mod Manager replaces the game's Modding page with one made for long mod lists: categories, profiles, a load order view, your own notes and tags, and a quick relaunch. The game's own list stays one click away.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]The public-beta branch, game version v0.111.0 or newer, for now.[/b] On the stable branch the game won't load it. To switch: right-click Slay the Spire 2 in your Steam library, then Properties, Betas, public-beta.
[*]No other mods needed.
[*]It doesn't change gameplay, so the people you play multiplayer with don't need it.
[/list]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Main menu button.[/b] "Spire Mod Manager" in the lower-left corner opens the page. Right-click it to move it. A dot shows when a relaunch is pending.
[*][b]Categories.[/b] Sort mods into your own collapsible categories, from a button on each row or the mod's right-click menu. Rename, move or delete a category from its header.
[*][b]Profiles.[/b] Save which mods are on and switch between sets. When the list differs from the saved profile, it shows "Unsaved" with Save, Save as new and Discard. Hover "Unsaved" to see exactly what changed. Switching to another profile keeps the unsaved changes with the one you left.
[*][b]Load Order view.[/b] Drag mods into order, one or several at a time, or use Top, Up, Down and Bottom. Lines show which mods need which. If a mod sits above a mod it needs, a warning offers Fix now. Auto sort puts libraries first, then gameplay mods, then visual mods, and keeps your order within each group.
[*][b]Your notes on each mod.[/b] Give a mod an alias, notes and your own tags. Edit them in the info panel or from the mod's right-click menu. Automatic tags are added for you: New, Local, Library, Gameplay and Cosmetic.
[*][b]Search.[/b] Searches names, aliases, notes, tags, authors, categories and Workshop tags. Type #tag to match a tag and @author to match an author. Click a tag or an author to search for it, or Shift-click to add it. Ctrl+F jumps to the search box.
[*][b]Select several mods.[/b] Ctrl-click, Shift-click or Ctrl+A. Then right-click to set their category, tags or notes together, or turn them all on or off.
[*][b]Changes, undo and redo.[/b] The bar at the bottom counts what changed since the game started. Click it for the full list. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo. Revert all puts things back the way they were when you opened the page.
[*][b]Relaunch Game.[/b] Restarts the game in place, in the same window mode, so your changes apply without going back through Steam. It checks first for mods that won't load (a mod they need is off or missing) and offers to turn on what they need or turn them off.
[*][b]Workshop details in the info panel.[/b] Published and updated dates, size, subscribers, Workshop tags, supported branches and a link to the mod's change notes. Problems, such as a missing dependency, show first in red.
[*][b]Vanilla List.[/b] The game's own Modding page, unchanged, one click away.
[/list]

[h2]Better Mod Menu[/h2]
Both mods can be on at the same time.
[list]
[*]The first time it runs, Spire Mod Manager copies Better Mod Menu's groups, aliases, notes and profiles. Better Mod Menu's own file is never changed.
[*]Better Mod Menu's page takes the place of the game's list. Open it with the Better Mod Menu button at the bottom of the page.
[*]The two keep separate profiles. Changes here also change Better Mod Menu's current profile, and switching its profile shows up here as unsaved changes. Our profiles never turn Better Mod Menu on or off.
[*]With both on, a warning on the page says some things may behave unexpectedly. Both mods change the same page. If something looks wrong, try again with one of them off, and tell me what happened.
[*]Better Mod Menu 1.1.1 has some errors of its own on the beta branch, with or without this mod.
[/list]

[h2]Your data[/h2]
Categories, aliases, notes, tags and profiles are saved in one file per Steam account. On Windows:
[code]%APPDATA%\SlayTheSpire2\steam\(your Steam ID)\mod_data\SpireModManager\manager.json[/code]
The first save of each session makes a backup in the backups folder next to it. The last 10 are kept.
This file is not in Steam Cloud, so it doesn't follow you to another PC or a Steam Deck.
Which mods are on, and their load order, stay where the game keeps them. Spire Mod Manager changes the same list as the game's own Modding page.

[h2]Uninstalling[/h2]
Unsubscribe here. The game's own Modding page keeps working: your mods stay on or off as you last set them, in the same load order. The data folder above stays behind. Delete it if you want everything gone.

[h2]Controls[/h2]
Mouse and keyboard only for now. Controller support may come later.

[h2]Bugs and ideas[/h2]
Post in the comments below. It helps to include:
[list]
[*]your game version and branch;
[*]what you did, and what happened;
[*]your log file, %APPDATA%\SlayTheSpire2\logs\godot.log (it can show your Windows user name in file paths).
[/list]
The source code isn't public yet. Once it is, a GitHub link for bug reports will go here.

[h2]Known limits[/h2]
[list]
[*]Public-beta branch only, for now. That changes once v0.111.0 or newer reaches the stable branch.
[*]Slay the Spire 2 is in Early Access. A game update can break parts of this mod until a fix is out.
[*]Other mod managers change the same page. Only Better Mod Menu has been tested alongside it, so use one manager at a time otherwise.
[*]Relaunch Game is tested on Windows only. macOS, Linux and Steam Deck are untested.
[*]Your data stays on this PC (see Your data).
[*]English only for now.
[/list]
